quote: Theorem 1. Let Xi ∼ M(θi), i = 1, 2 be two random variables. If θ1 ≤ θ2, then X1 ≺lr X2, X1 ≺hr X2, X1 ≺s X2 and X1 ≺cx X2. Proof. We have fX1(t)/fX2(t) = [θ1³(1+θ2)/(θ2³(1+θ1))] e^{−(θ1−θ2)t}. differentiating w.r.t t, we get (d/dt)[fX1(t)/fX2(t)] = −(θ1 − θ2)e^{−(θ1−θ2)t} < 0, ∀θ1 ≥ θ2. Hence, we see that fX1(t)/fX2(t) decreases in t, which holds the above theorem. (proved)
